rationale: This is a denominator swap (invt/cogs instead of invt/at) on the already-tested LowMarginInventoryAcceleration, a cosmetic variant of an archived signal rather than a new mechanism.

It simply splices the archived funding-gap term onto the margin-drawdown conditioner from CapacityBuildAfterMarginPeak — the very conditioner that produced a strong FMB t-stat but essentially zero FF5 alpha (0.007, t=0.64) — so it replaces a working portfolio conditioner (margin level, alpha −0.052) with one already shown to fail at the portfolio level.

A three-way recombination of existing archive blocks (PPE build, external-financing term, margin-drawdown gate) that again relies on the drawdown conditioner with no demonstrated alpha, and the MIN gate will further thin an already ~0.08–0.13 coverage universe without a distinct economic story.

The pairing of an inventory-stock overhang state (rather than one-period growth) with debt-financed accumulation at weak-cash-flow firms is a coherent distress-inventory mechanism not yet tested, though it is a formulaic reuse of two working templates and coverage attrition from the MIN gate should be monitored.

This bolts a debt-growth MIN gate onto the already-archived AccrualBackedNonGoodwillIntangibles (coverage only 0.067, alpha −0.032, t=−3.23), which risks shrinking coverage below usability for a marginal, weakly motivated increment — intangible additions are typically acquisition- or capitalization-driven rather than directly debt-funded.

It is a one-component swap on the archived ShortTermFundedLowMarginInventory template (capex acceleration for inventory growth), and the capex-ramp × short-term-liquidity-strain interaction was already tested as LiquidityPressedCapexRamp and delivered a wrong-signed alpha (+0.018).
